verdicts.dateTest: Tekchand Sawarkar, sitting BJP MLA for Kamthi (2019 to 2024 term), told a public meeting the scheme was a "jugaad" for women's votes on Tuesday 24 Sep 2024. PTI/Deccan Herald published at 2024-09-25T16:27 IST and India TV at 2024-09-25T12:38 IST. He was still in office, so the dates overlap. The remark came after the budget announcement (28 Jun 2024), the first instalments (Aug 2024, before Raksha Bandhan) and the Bombay HC ruling (5 Aug 2024), and before the Nov 2024 poll. The edge's `from: 2024-09-25` is the publication date, not the date he spoke, which was 24 Sep 2024.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. PTI names "Tekchand Sawarkar, who represents the Kamthi assembly seat in Nagpur district." India TV also names him as the Kamthi MLA. The node's office field ("MLA Kamthi, 2019→2024") matches. One small conflict: PTI says he spoke "in his constituency" (Kamthi), while India TV says it was "a meeting in the Mauda assembly constituency of Nagpur district." Neither outlet says whether he was talking about the scheme as a government insider or as a campaigner. He is a backbench MLA, not the CM, Deputy CM or minister who designed the scheme.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a single statement, so a scheme-level base rate does not apply directly. The relevant reference class is ruling-party politicians asking for votes in return for welfare they have delivered. That is close to universal in Indian campaigns across all parties (for example, MP Ladli Behna in 2023, and Congress guarantees in Karnataka and Telangana, where leaders openly tie the benefit to the vote). The remark is unusual only because he says outright that vote-winning was the purpose ("why else would we do it?"). As proof of how the government decided on the scheme, it tells us very little.
verdicts.denialFound: None found (searched). There is no retraction or clarification from Sawarkar and no BJP or Mahayuti rebuttal of this specific remark, either in the PTI/DH or India TV reports or in web search. Neither report says the MLA or the party was asked for comment. The nearest thing to a government response is general and came earlier: CM Shinde at the launch said people "must not fall prey to the fake narrative of the opposition about the Ladki Bahin Yojana" (quoted in India TV, https://www.indiatvnews.com/maharashtra/bjp-mla-controversial-statement-on-ladki-bahin-yojana-maharashtra-government-assembly-elections-2024-opposition-reactions-latest-updates-2024-09-25-953893).
verdicts.innocentReading: This was stump rhetoric at a local rally. A backbench MLA claimed credit for a popular benefit and asked beneficiaries to vote for the lotus, which is how every incumbent campaigns on delivered welfare. He was not describing how the cabinet actually decided. The scheme was announced in the regular 2024-25 budget, and the MP Ladli Behna model had already been copied across states. Nothing in the reports shows that his view reflects how the scheme was really designed.
verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. PTI via Deccan Herald (by-line PTI, 25 Sep 2024) quotes: "We came up with this jugaad (ploy) of Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana to ensure women vote for the BJP. Tell me honestly, why else would we do it? Because during polls, my dear sisters will vote for the BJP." He added that "our only 'swarth' (motive) is to get votes," and LoP Vijay Wadettiwar shared the video clip on X. India TV independently reports the same clip with a different translation. That the remark was made is therefore solid: two outlets plus a circulated video, strong enough on its own for reported or even documented. The edge is framed as an allegation about the scheme's vote-buying intent, so alleged is the right tier. It is a named party's statement, and it cannot be documented, because one MLA's rally speech does not establish what the government intended. The weak point is the contra. c019, the Bombay HC ruling of 5 Aug 2024, came seven weeks before the remark. According to the DH text it dealt with a PIL about the burden on taxpayers ("It is a policy decision, so we cannot interfere unless there is violation of any fundamental rights"). It never considered electoral inducement or motive. "Not discriminatory" appears only in DH's headline. Legal validity does not answer electoral intent, so the claim wrongly joins two true facts as if one rebuts the other.

Note that it places the meeting in Mauda, not Kamthi. (4) c019: it does not rebut c017. Relabel it along the lines of "court: scheme is a policy decision beyond judicial interference (fiscal-burden PIL); did not address electoral motive". Delete the `d` text "institutional answer to the 'inducement' framing", which overstates what the ruling covered. Mark "not discriminatory" as DH's headline wording, not the court's quoted holding. If a real contra is needed, use Shinde's "fake narrative of the opposition" statement, or the Lokniti-CSDS finding already in the narrative that there is "hardly any connection between welfare and vote." (5) The claim text's "contra c019" clause should not suggest that the HC ruling responded to the remark, since the ruling came first.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the PM (with the Nitish Kumar-led Bihar govt) transferred Rs 10,000 each to 75 lakh women (Rs 7,500 cr) on 26 Sep 2025. The cited PIB release (PRID 2171342, posted 25 SEP 2025 6:44PM) says, before the event: "Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will launch Bihar's Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana on September 26 at 11 AM via video conferencing... will also directly transfer Rs. 10,000 each into the bank accounts of 75 lakh women across Bihar, totaling Rs. 7,500 crore." ANI, DD News and Swarajya reports dated 26 Sep 2025 confirm the transfer happened. The ECI/PIB release of 6 Oct 2025 (PRID 2175533) gives the assembly term as "23-11-2020 to 22-11-2025", which matches the innocent reading. 26 Sep to 6 Oct is 10 days (correct). Phase 1 polling was 6 Nov, so the gap is 41 days, about 6 weeks (correct). Deccan Herald (last updated 14 Nov 2025) has the NDA at 202. Nitish Kumar was CM throughout and Modi was PM, so the tenures overlap. Omissions: cabinet approval was 29 Aug 2025 (the record has approved.date null), and the portal/application launch was about 7 Sep 2025 (newsonair).
verdicts.identityTest: Scheme identity holds. PIB names "Bihar's Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana", "an initiative of the Government of Bihar", launched by PM Narendra Modi. The CM and PM office-holders are correct for the dates. Record-ID mismatch: in /home/user/india-corporate-intelligence/research/raw/welfare/women-cash.json the id women-cash:c057 belongs to a different claim, a Haryana edge (wel:nayab-singh-saini role -> scheme:hr-lado-lakshmi). The Bihar claim actually sits in scheme:br-mukhyamantri-mahila-rozgar results[0] and has no claim id of its own. Also, the NDA of 2020 (125 = BJP 74, JD(U) 43, VIP 4, HAM 4) had different members from the NDA of 2025 (202, including LJP(RV) 19, which contested separately in 2020, while VIP had left). So "125 to 202" is a like-for-like label on a coalition whose membership changed.
verdicts.baseRate: The pre-poll timing does not discriminate. In this file, the incumbent-run women-cash schemes that paid money before an election cover every party: MP Ladli Behna (BJP, 2023), Maharashtra Ladki Bahin (Mahayuti, 2024), Jharkhand Maiya Samman (JMM, opposition, 2024) and Bihar MMRY (NDA, 2025). Essentially 100% of incumbents who had such a scheme paid out before polling, and all of those incumbents won. What does set Bihar apart is scale and concentration: Rs 7,500 cr in one day, then roughly 1.41 crore women paid by 31 Oct (Amit Shah, per Business Standard/Outlook), with tranches on 3 Oct (25 lakh women, Rs 2,500 cr, newsonair), 6 Oct, and 17, 24 and 31 Oct, plus one planned for 7 Nov. The closest comparison in the file, Maharashtra's advance Oct+Nov instalments in Oct 2024, was also about Rs 7,000 cr but spread over several days. So "largest single-day pre-poll transfer in the file" holds, narrowly. Symmetry check: the same lens applied to the JMM in Jharkhand (opposition party, pre-poll Maiya Samman increase, won) gives the same reading, so the lens is not partisan.
verdicts.denialFound: Not a denial of the facts, but a response on legitimacy exists. RJD MP Manoj Jha wrote to the ECI alleging MCC violation over the transfers on 17, 24 and 31 Oct and the planned 7 Nov transfer (Business Standard https://www.business-standard.com/elections/bihar-elections/rjd-s-manoj-jha-writes-to-ec-accuses-bihar-govt-of-mcc-violation-125103101715_1.html; Outlook https://www.outlookindia.com/elections/rjds-manoj-jha-accuses-bihar-government-of-violating-mcc-with-pre-poll-cash-transfers). Unnamed "informed official sources" answered that there was no violation because the scheme was approved by the Bihar cabinet on 29 Aug 2025 and launched on 26 Sep, before the MCC started on 6 Oct (ETV Bharat https://www.etvbharat.com/en/bharat/rjd-leader-writes-to-ec-says-bihar-govt-violated-mcc-by-transferring-money-to-women-ahead-of-poll-enn25110100014). None of this is in the record.
verdicts.innocentReading: The assembly term ended on 22 Nov 2025 (confirmed in the ECI release), so any benefit launched after mid-2025 would fall inside the poll window. The scheme is designed as livelihood seed capital through the existing JEEVIKA SHG network, with up to Rs 2 lakh more in later phases tied to business progress, not an open-ended monthly cash payment. Cabinet approval (29 Aug) and the launch came before the MCC. The NDA swing has many other plausible causes: coalition realignment (LJP(RV) back in the NDA), the SIR roll revision, and anti-incumbency against the opposition alliance. No study isolates the effect of MMRY.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives because every hard fact checks out against sources. Rs 7,500 cr to 75 lakh women on 26 Sep 2025 comes from the PIB release (which says "will"), and 26 Sep news reports confirm it was paid. The ECI release confirms the 6 Oct schedule and the 22 Nov 2025 term end. Deccan Herald confirms the NDA's 202 seats. The claim is a set of true facts put side by side that suggest a causal link ("paid, then won big"), which is exactly what the analytic tier covers, and the claim carries the required innocent reading. Timing alone does not discriminate (every party in the file does pre-poll payouts); the claim rests on scale, and the "largest in the file" superlative holds. Problems that need correcting rather than killing: (a) the claim's only cited source is a forward-looking PIB release that does not mention the ECI date, polling, 125 or 202; (b) the 2020 figure of 125 is not sourced anywhere; (c) the id c057 points to a different record; (d) the claim leaves out the larger pre-poll programme (about 1.41 crore women paid by 31 Oct, including tranches during the MCC) and the RJD complaint with the official reply, which is the actual response on record.
